name: West Bank: settler violence and Israeli military operations
summary: Settler attacks on Palestinians hit a record 1,835 in 2025 and were running faster still in 2026, while Israel accelerates settlement approvals including the E1 project east of Jerusalem. Deaths are lower than in 2024 but violence and land loss are more widespread.

sides.name: Israeli forces and settlers
members: Armed settler groups and outpost youth
backers: Israeli government ministers backing settlement expansion (e.g. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich)
leaders: Bezalel Smotrich (Finance Minister, also responsible for settlement civil administration)

sides.name: Palestinian armed groups and communities
members: Local armed cells in northern camps (Jenin, Tulkarm, Nur Shams)
Palestinian Authority security forces (not party to fighting with Israel, but a political actor)

background: Violence in the occupied West Bank surged after 7 October 2023, with large Israeli raids on armed groups in the northern refugee camps and a sharp rise in settler attacks on Palestinian villages and herding communities. In January 2025 the IDF launched an extended operation in the Jenin, Tulkarm and Nur Shams camps that displaced tens of thousands.

The second Netanyahu-Smotrich era has also brought structural changes: new settlements, legalised outposts, and the E1 plan that would link Ma'ale Adumim to Jerusalem and, critics say, cut the West Bank in two. This matters because it shapes whether any Palestinian state remains geographically possible.
year: UN agencies recorded a record month of settler attacks in October 2025, and OCHA counted 1,835 incidents for the whole of 2025. In January-April 2026 attacks averaged about 190 a month, displacing nearly 700 Palestinians from nine communities. By 20 July 2026, 18 Palestinians had been killed in settler-related incidents that year. Late July brought a cluster of violence in which eight Palestinians and two Israelis were killed in a few days. Between 13 June and 18 September 2026 the UN counted 32 Palestinians killed, including nine children.

On the political track, E1 tenders for 1,234 housing units were published on 18 August 2026, about 4,570 settlement units were advanced in Area C and 3,515 in East Jerusalem in the reporting period, and Smotrich announced new settlements. Canada, France and the UK banned settlement goods on 8 September, and Israel retaliated by ordering the UK consulate in East Jerusalem closed. Israel continues to withhold tax revenue from the Palestinian Authority.
situation: As of mid-September 2026 OCHA had logged more than 1,600 settler attacks with casualties or damage in 2026, about 6.7 a day versus 5 a day in 2025. E1 tender awards are frozen until after the 27 October election by an Attorney-General ruling. The PA is in a deep fiscal crisis.
technical: OCHA: 1,835 settler attacks in 2025; more than 1,600 in 2026 by 14 Sep (6.7/day vs 5/day) (UN News Jul 2026; Security Council Report Oct 2026).
OHCHR projected more than 2,000 settler attacks in 2026 at the Jan-Apr rate of about 190/month (UN News, 29 Jul 2026).
Of 18 Palestinians killed in settler-related incidents in 2026 by 20 Jul: 12 by settlers, 3 by Israeli forces, 3 disputed (UN News, 29 Jul 2026).

E1: 3,401 approved units on about 12 sq km between East Jerusalem and Ma'ale Adumim; tenders for 1,234 published 18 Aug 2026, bid deadline 19 Oct, no award before 27 Oct election (Security Council Report).
Settlement planning in the period: about 4,570 units in Area C and 3,515 in East Jerusalem (Security Council Report).
8 Sep 2026: Canada, France, UK ban settlement-goods imports; nine more states join a joint statement; Israel orders UK consulate in East Jerusalem closed (Security Council Report).
Israeli forces entered an UNRWA training centre in East Jerusalem for a second time on 28 Jul 2026 (UN News).
casualties: UN: 32 Palestinians killed, including 9 children, between 13 Jun and 18 Sep 2026 (Security Council Report, Oct 2026); 18 killed in settler-related incidents in 2026 as of 20 Jul (UN News, 29 Jul 2026). A full Oct 2025-Oct 2026 total was not retrieved. Israeli deaths include two killed in late July 2026 (UN News).
displaced: Nearly 700 Palestinians displaced from nine communities by settler attacks in Jan-Apr 2026 (OHCHR via UN News, 29 Jul 2026). Displacement from the northern camps since Jan 2025 not re-verified for 2026.

timeline.event: UN reports October 2025 as a record month for settler attacks.
Jan-Apr 2026 settler attacks average about 190 a month; nearly 700 displaced.
UN Security Council briefing on surge in killings; eight Palestinians and two Israelis killed in preceding days.
Tenders published for 1,234 E1 housing units.
Canada, France, UK ban settlement goods; Israel orders UK East Jerusalem consulate closed.
OCHA count passes 1,600 settler attacks for 2026.

outlook: Watch whether the post-election government awards the E1 tenders, any formal annexation steps (opposed publicly by the US), the PA's fiscal collapse and security-force cohesion, and whether settler violence keeps rising toward the projected 2,000-plus incidents for 2026.
